subject.title: Feature request: Coalesce interleaved text blocks into single outbound message

question: Should tool-interleaved assistant text in channel sessions be coalesced into one message, delivered final-only, suppressed until explicit message-tool sends, or delivered progressively at tool boundaries, and should that be a new config option or a default policy change?
rationale: The current source confirms the gap, but each fix shape changes cross-channel delivery semantics and config surface area, and related issues ask for conflicting outcomes.

options.title: Define opt-in coalescing/final-only policy
options.body: Add an explicit shared reply-pipeline mode that defaults existing users to current behavior while allowing Telegram/iMessage-style users to reduce multi-message bursts.

options.title: Keep current defaults and document existing controls
options.body: Treat current canonical-final-answer cleanup plus blockStreamingCoalesce as the supported behavior and avoid adding another config surface for now.

options.title: Route to explicit-send/suppression design
options.body: Fold this into the broader messaging-channel policy discussion where bare assistant text becomes internal unless the message tool explicitly sends it.

recommendation.title: Define opt-in coalescing/final-only policy
recommendation.body: Add an explicit shared reply-pipeline mode that defaults existing users to current behavior while allowing Telegram/iMessage-style users to reduce multi-message bursts.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal across the block coalescer, tool-boundary flush behavior, and prior maintainer review of this exact issue.
